title: Diagnose isolated test_application.py finalization abort
description:
## Symptom
Running `xvfb-run uv run --no-sync pytest -q doorstop_edit/test/test_application.py` completes all 26 assertions, then aborts with exit 134 during CPython finalization (`none_dealloc`). The complete local Xvfb suite passes (69 tests); CI currently runs the full suite, not this test module by itself.

## Impact
Observed impact is limited to the isolated test process and its unusable exit status. No normal app crash or user data loss has been demonstrated. Production impact is unverified, so treat it as low observed impact—not proven absent. Raise priority and investigate sooner if the abort appears during normal app use or affects full-suite CI.

## Evidence / investigation
A cumulative 22-test selection reproduces after its assertions; smaller subsets pass. Regular symbols-enabled and Py_DEBUG CPython 3.11.14 builds reproduce at finalization. GDB sees `_Py_NoneStruct.ob_refcnt` reach zero during cleanup, but the immediate object varies and no native extension owner is identified. No speculative source fix is supported.

## Deferred follow-up
Resume once the app is operational, provided no user-facing crash/data-loss impact has emerged. First preserve a fresh-process repro, minimize the ordered test selection, compare teardown/refcount/native-module state, then rebuild only implicated native extensions with symbols. Require repeatable clean isolated runs and a passing full suite for any fix.
close_reason: Diagnosed the isolated finalization abort to PySide 6.12.0 cross-version singleton ownership behavior from Python 3.12 headers; provenance/callsite limits documented, 6.11.3 workaround verified

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Local operational gate met: Xvfb smoke test showed the window and loaded 2 sample documents / 10 items. Resuming isolated test-abort diagnosis; no user-facing crash has been demonstrated.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: 2026-11-03 update: local Xvfb smoke test showed the app window and loaded 2 sample documents / 10 items, so the operational gate for resuming this test-only investigation was met. Three fresh runs of the full test_application.py each passed all 26 tests then exited 134 with none_dealloc. Bounded order-preserving minimization found a 20-test subset that also reproduces after all assertions; it was reproduced twice. A wider automated minimization exceeded its 10-minute bound without identifying a unique test or root cause. No source fix was made; outputs are under /tmp/opencode/doorstop-ddmin and /tmp/opencode/doorstop-test-application-fresh*.log.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: 2026-11-03 differential probe update: compared the reproducing 20-test subset with the same ordered selection minus test_remove_leaf_refreshes_selection_and_editor (19 tests, clean exit). At pytest sessionfinish, both had the same 20 native-extension module paths, same enumerated Python threads, and identical Qt widget census (203 widgets, all hidden). The `None` refcount snapshots differed between runs but are not alone causal evidence. This does not implicate the leaf test or a native extension; no root cause found. Probe code and JSONL logs remain under /tmp/opencode.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: 2026-11-03 probe follow-up: pytest-session snapshots for the failing 20-test selection and passing 19-test selection (minus the leaf-removal test) had identical native extension sets, thread states, and Qt widget counts/types. This did not isolate a native owner. Attempting to arm a hardware watchpoint on None from process startup was too slow because the refcount is written frequently; an initial pre-relocation attempt watched the wrong address. The earlier finalization-only watchpoint remains the useful bounded GDB result. No project code changes.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: 2026-11-05 diagnosis: Closed at mechanism/cause-class level. Existing fresh-process A/B reproduces  after 26 tests on Python 3.11/PySide6 6.12.0 and passes on 6.11.3; helper lifecycle is not causal. An unmodified PySide v6.12.0 source build using CPython 3.12.12 headers + Py_LIMITED_API 3.10 loses one True reference per discarded Signal.emit()/isinstance result on Python 3.11, while Python 3.12 is balanced; changing only those return pairs to Py_NewRef fixes the source-build probe. A standalone extension also confirms the same 3.12-header macro behavior for Py_RETURN_NONE, explaining how the identical ownership defect can cause none_dealloc. Exact  application call site and PyPI wheel-to-Coin build provenance remain unverified; do not state those as proven. Keep PySide6 6.11.3 workaround; no Doorstop fix, Qt issue submission, or commit. Full research: /home/digi4care/projects/opencode-agents/research/2026-11-03-doorstop-edit-render-shutdown-followup.md

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Correction/addendum to diagnosis comment: the fatal is `none_dealloc` after all 26 application tests under Python 3.11/PySide6 6.12.0. The standalone macro probe specifically tested `Py_RETURN_NONE` and lost one None reference per discarded result; the exact call site in the application remains unidentified. Public Coin data identifies a matching release-branch integration but does not tie it to the exact PyPI wheel hash or expose its build interpreter/command. Cause class is strongly supported by the actual PySide source A/B; exact artifact provenance is not asserted.

title: Review baseline testing and code standards
description:
Review Doorstop Edit’s existing automated tests and code against basic programming standards. Cover test coverage/automation, algorithm and data-structure complexity (Big O) where relevant, code quality, security, performance, and architectural boundaries.

Scope constraints:
- Do not rewrite or broadly refactor the application.
- Keep recommendations proportionate to this small application; focus on basic, actionable standards.
- Do not add heavyweight tools or dependencies without a separate issue/approval.

Acceptance criteria:
- Run the existing automated test and code-check workflows; record the commands and results.
- Review representative and risk-sensitive code paths for correctness, Big O/complexity where applicable, security, performance, and architecture.
- Identify missing tests or basic automated checks that would catch concrete issues.
- Produce a concise, prioritized findings report with file/symbol references and evidence; distinguish verified defects from recommendations.
- Create separate follow-up issues for actionable fixes or broader changes; make no broad rewrites as part of this review.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Use Doorstop for traceability: link applicable quality requirements to automated tests and review evidence/findings, and report uncovered or untestable requirements. Apply basic software quality-assurance principles without claiming compliance with a formal standard.
close_reason: Review is complete; four follow-up issues remain open by design. Report and research note record evidence and untestable Doorstop traceability.

description: Modernize the Python developer quality-tool stack as a separate follow-up to dependency/Python support Bead .9. Replace Black, autoflake, isort, and Flake8 with Ruff's formatter, import sorter, and lint rules while preserving the project's intended checks and formatting conventions. Evaluate a faster, actively maintained type checker (for example Astral ty) as a replacement for mypy; do not weaken the current type-checking coverage or strictness. Update pyproject.toml, uv.lock, tools/check_code.py, CI, and developer documentation. Compare check runtime against the current toolchain where practical; record any unsupported check or reason to retain an existing tool.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Ruff replaces Black, autoflake, isort, and Flake8 in dependency declarations, configuration, local code checks, and CI; preserve equivalent project rules and formatting behavior.
- [x] Evaluate a modern type-checker replacement for mypy against the project's current mypy strictness and diagnostics; replace mypy only if coverage is not weakened, otherwise document the concrete gap and keep it explicitly.
- [x] Regenerate uv.lock and verify the declared tools install on every supported Python version.
- [x] Run the new code-check workflow and pytest suite on supported Python versions; report any differences from the prior toolchain.
- [x] Update contributor/setup documentation; do not mix in application behavior changes.
notes:
Ruff migration applied: replaced Black/autoflake/isort/Flake8 with Ruff; mypy retained. Initial check found import-order/format findings, now being corrected and revalidated.
Completed: Ruff replaces Black/autoflake/isort/Flake8; mypy retained because no equivalent ty setup has been proven for the configured strictness and PySide/generated UI imports. acceptance_criteria: A bounded subprocess reproducer establishes current behavior for a normal and intentionally blocking validator; results are captured in research notes; options/trade-offs and the user decision still required are recorded; no production behavior changed.

title: Audit dependencies and modernize Python support
description: Audit the app’s runtime, development, and build dependencies, and reassess the Python versions the app claims to support. PySide6 6.12 supports Python >=3.10,<3.16, so the existing Python 3.9–3.11 range should not be retained merely for historical reasons. Verify the whole dependency set, platform wheel availability, and app behavior before adopting a newer range. Update compatible dependencies, uv.lock, CI, docs, and changelog; keep application features and unrelated refactors out of this issue.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Inventory runtime, development, and build dependencies and verify whether each is used and still required.
- [x] Evaluate the current Python support range against current PySide6 and every direct/transitive dependency, including platform wheel availability and the CI OS matrix; do not preserve Python 3.9 automatically.
- [x] Recommend a modern supported Python range based on evidence. Where the dependency set and app tests support it, raise the minimum and upper bound and update CI to test the selected range; document any versions deliberately excluded.
- [x] Update compatible dependencies and regenerate uv.lock; document packages intentionally held back and reasons.
- [x] Run tests, code checks, and package builds across the selected Python range and supported OS matrix; report regressions.
- [x] Update setup/dependency docs and changelog; keep app feature work separate.
notes:
User approved the modern dependency/platform stack: target Python 3.11–3.14 with current compatible dependencies; accept PySide6 6.12 platform floors (macOS 14+, Linux glibc 2.34+ x86-64 / 2.39+ ARM64). Update CI/docs accordingly and validate before claiming support.
Validation update: uv lock --check passes; tools/check_code.py passes Black/autoflake/isort/Flake8/mypy after updating Watchdog 7 event typing/path decoding and removing stale type ignores. Linux pytest passes 23/23 on Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14 with isolated HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME. Previous package check confirmed wheel/sdist metadata Requires-Python >=3.11,<3.15 and required generated resources. YAML/bash syntax and git diff --check pass. macOS/Windows CI and GUI/platform acceptance remain unverified; issue stays in_progress.
Follow-up after Ruff Bead .11: code checks are now Ruff + mypy and pass on Linux Python 3.11–3.14; pytest remains 23/23 on each. `uv sync --locked --dry-run --no-install-project` passed for Python 3.11–3.14 on Windows x86_64, Linux x86_64 manylinux_2_34, and Linux ARM64 manylinux_2_39. uv.lock includes PySide6 cp310-abi3 wheel records/hashes for macOS 14 universal2, Linux and Windows. macOS cross-dry-run from Linux maps to macOS 13 and cannot validate the macOS 14 wheel; no GitHub Actions runs exist for this uncommitted branch. A real Watchdog 7 Linux observer smoke test reported external YAML create/modify. Keep item 5 and issue open pending actual macOS/Windows hosted CI/platform validation and full matrix package builds.
Additional local evidence: wheel/sdist builds succeeded at Python 3.11 and 3.14; both include generated UI/build-info files and Requires-Python >=3.11,<3.15. Application remained running for six seconds under Xvfb on Python 3.14 with no startup exception. This does not replace manual GUI workflow acceptance or hosted macOS/Windows CI.
Package build coverage extended: `uv build --python` succeeded for each Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14; inspected wheel/sdist metadata and generated resources. Cross-platform CI remains the sole unmet automated matrix item.

title: Requirements checker scans nested worktrees as extra requirement roots
description:
## Symptom
`QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen uv run pytest -q` fails `test_uncovered_requirements_are_reported_without_failure`. The test invokes `tools/check_requirements.py`, which reports two Doorstop root documents: the intended `requirements/REQ` tree and the bundled fixture under `.slim/worktrees/qml-python-prototype/prototypes/qml-python/fixture/REQ`.

## Evidence
Directly running the checker produces `Invalid Doorstop requirements tree: multiple root documents`. In installed Doorstop 3.2, `doorstop.build(cwd=str(TREE), root=str(TREE))` builds exactly one `REQ` document, while the current call `doorstop.build(str(TREE))` finds the repository root and recursively scans nested worktrees. Resolution: fixed by passing the requirements directory as both cwd and root; see the resolution notes and regression test below.

## Scope
Fix the checker scan boundary without suppressing validation or hiding broken requirement links. Preserve source/evidence/native-reference checks and uncovered/untestable reporting. The full test run also emitted a Qt WebEnginePage teardown warning and exited 139; that is a separate, not-yet-isolated symptom and is not assumed fixed by this issue.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Keep a nested Doorstop document at `.slim/worktrees/qml-python-prototype/prototypes/qml-python/fixture/REQ`.
2. Run `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen uv run pytest -q` or `uv run python tools/check_requirements.py` from the repository root.
3. Observe that the checker fails because Doorstop discovers both the intended requirements tree and the nested fixture as roots.

## Expected Result
The project checker validates only the configured `requirements/` tree, independently of unrelated nested worktrees.


## Resolution
Updated `tools/check_requirements.py` to call Doorstop with `cwd= TREE` and `root= TREE`; added a nested-root regression test. Focused tests pass. The separate exit-139 symptom is tracked under Beads issue `doorstop-edit-qml-frontend-migration-plan-lml.12`.
acceptance_criteria: The checker scans only the intended requirements tree even when a nested worktree contains another Doorstop REQ root; add a regression test for that scenario; the existing requirements-checker tests pass; broken source/evidence/reference links still fail and uncovered requirements remain reported.
notes:
Fixed by scoping Doorstop to `requirements/` via `doorstop.build(cwd=str(TREE), root=str(TREE))` and adding `test_checker_ignores_nested_doorstop_root`. Focused checker suite: 5 passed; direct checker exits 0 and reports the existing uncovered REQs; Ruff check/format pass. Full suite after fix: 72 passed, but process still exits 139 after Qt WebEnginePage teardown warning. That separate finalization symptom is tracked in a new issue.
Follow-up: after the independent Qt test-harness fix in , the full suite now reports 72 passed and exits 0.  itself remains limited to explicit requirements-root scope and its regression test.
Correction: after the independent Qt test-harness fix tracked in Beads issue doorstop-edit-qml-frontend-migration-plan-lml.12, the full suite now reports 72 passed and exits 0. This issue remains limited to explicit requirements-root scope and its regression test.
close_reason: Checker scope fixed; nested-root regression test and existing requirements-checker tests pass.

title: Full pytest suite exits 139 after successful assertions under PySide6 6.11.3
description:
## Symptom
After fixing the requirements-checker nested-root failure, `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen uv run pytest -q` reports all 72 tests passed, then prints `Release of profile requested but WebEnginePage still not deleted. Expect troubles !` and the process exits with status 139.

## Environment and evidence
Python 3.11.14, PySide6 6.11.3, Qt 6.11.3. The failure persists after the checker test passes, so it is independent of the duplicate Doorstop root assertion. No user-facing application crash is demonstrated. A prior closed issue `doorstop-edit-7cc` diagnosed a different isolated finalization abort on PySide6 6.12.0 and documented 6.11.3 as a workaround; this full-suite result may be related but must not be assumed to have the same cause.

## Scope
Preserve a fresh-process reproduction, establish whether the WebEnginePage/profile warning is causal, isolate teardown ownership/order, and avoid speculative fixes. Separate test-runner teardown from production behavior.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Use the recorded environment: Python 3.11.14, PySide6 6.11.3, Qt 6.11.3.
2. Run `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen uv run pytest -q` from the repository root after the requirements-checker fix.
3. Observe all 72 tests pass, followed by the Qt WebEngine profile/page teardown warning and process exit status 139.


## Resolution
The reproducible failure was in the test harness path: `test_start_no_exceptions` constructs the application without entering `QApplication.exec()`, then calls `DoorstopEdit.quit()`, which schedules `QWebEnginePage.deleteLater()` but the fixture did not flush deferred-delete events. The test alone reproduced the profile/page warning and exit 139. The fixture now uses `try/finally`, calls app shutdown, sends `QEvent.DeferredDelete`, and processes Qt events. The focused test, `test_main.py`, and the complete 72-test suite then exit 0. This establishes a test-runner cleanup issue; it does not establish a production application crash or require production code changes.
acceptance_criteria: The full test suite exits 0 after assertions on the supported local Qt/Python matrix; if the failure is version/platform-specific, the cause and safe supported matrix are evidenced; regression test protects cleanup; no user-facing crash impact or fix is claimed without evidence.
notes: Reproduced with only `test_start_no_exceptions`: 1 passed, then profile/page teardown warning and exit 139. After the test fixture explicitly flushes deferred deletes, that single test and `test_main.py` both exit 0; full suite is 72 passed and exits 0. Ruff check/format pass. No production code changed; normal-user impact remains unproven and is not claimed.
close_reason: Full suite now exits 0; isolated reproducer and test module pass after Qt deferred-delete cleanup in the no-event-loop test harness.

Preserve existing behavior and use docs/qml-frontend-migration-plan.md plus the approved capability baseline. Do not change unrelated production behavior or remove a Widgets workflow without explicit approval.

title: Build migration requirements traceability knowledge graph
description:
Create a machine-readable and reviewable graph linking requirements, existing UI capabilities, source symbols/files, tests, Beads epics/stories and verification evidence. See docs/qml-frontend-migration-plan.md.

## Success Criteria

- Graph schema and provenance are documented; links can be generated or validated; missing/stale/uncovered links are reported; the graph supports impact queries and never falsely claims formal compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Graph schema and provenance are documented; links can be generated or validated; missing/stale/uncovered links are reported; the graph supports impact queries and never falsely claims formal compliance.

title: Traceability Graph Schema And Provenance
description:
User story: As a maintainer, I want a versioned graph schema for requirements, frontend capabilities, code, tests, Beads issues and evidence.

Preserve existing behavior and use docs/qml-frontend-migration-plan.md plus the approved capability baseline. Do not change unrelated production behavior or remove a Widgets workflow without explicit approval.
acceptance_criteria: Define stable IDs and typed relationships, source citations/line references, provenance, status/freshness and schema version; document ontology boundaries and no-compliance claim.

title: Generate And Validate Traceability Graph
description:
User story: As a reviewer, I want trace links generated or validated so missing and stale coverage is visible.

acceptance_criteria: Build graph from Doorstop requirements, capability inventory, code/test evidence and Beads; checker fails broken links and reports uncovered/stale nodes; integrate into CI without imposing false coverage.

title: Traceability Impact And Review Views
description:

Preserve existing behavior and use docs/qml-frontend-migration-plan.md plus the approved capability baseline. Do not change unrelated production behavior or remove a Widgets workflow without explicit approval.
acceptance_criteria: Support paths requirement→capability→source→test→Beads and reverse impact; report cited results and update procedure; verify representative queries.

title: Define and deliver ontology-driven live app knowledge graph
description:
Specify ontology requirements and competency questions; expose an optional QML graph view over Doorstop documents/items/links/status/review/validation with live updates and navigation to existing editor/tree. See docs/qml-frontend-migration-plan.md.

## Success Criteria

- Ontology concepts/relations/provenance and update semantics are documented and validated; graph reflects local and watched external changes within an agreed latency; graph is optional, interoperable with existing workflows, and performance-tested on representative large projects.
acceptance_criteria: Ontology concepts/relations/provenance are documented; the first graph supports relationship exploration, impact analysis and live review/suspect-link/validation status; it is an optional in-memory projection with Doorstop as source of truth; local and watched external changes appear within 1 second; no graph database/persistent graph/RDF/OWL/JSON-LD in v1 absent a concrete need; performance is tested on representative large projects.
notes: User confirmed first-version scope: relationship exploration, impact analysis and live review/suspect-link/validation status. App-native typed ontology; derived in-memory graph; Doorstop stays source of truth; target visible update <=1s after local or watched external changes; no graph database/persistent storage/RDF/OWL/JSON-LD in v1 absent concrete need. See docs/qml-frontend-analysis.md §7.

title: Ontology Vocabulary And Competency Questions
description:
User story: As a user, I want a domain ontology grounded in real Doorstop workflows rather than invented labels.

Preserve existing behavior and use docs/qml-frontend-migration-plan.md plus the approved capability baseline. Do not change unrelated production behavior or remove a Widgets workflow without explicit approval.
acceptance_criteria: Use an app-native typed ontology for v1. Define detailed concepts/relations and provenance against Doorstop and all three approved graph goals; no mandatory RDF/OWL standard. Document any future interop use-case before expanding.
notes: User selected all three graph goals and an app-native typed ontology for v1. Define detailed domain terms and relation semantics against the actual Doorstop API; no RDF/OWL standard required for v1.

title: Doorstop To Graph Domain Adapter
description:
User story: As a user, I want a graph built from the existing Doorstop source of truth.

Preserve existing behavior and use docs/qml-frontend-migration-plan.md plus the approved capability baseline. Do not change unrelated production behavior or remove a Widgets workflow without explicit approval.
acceptance_criteria: Map documents/items/links/levels/attributes/review and validation evidence; use stable Doorstop IDs, preserve source paths and provenance, handle invalid/missing/cyclic data; no duplicate editable truth.

title: Live Graph Consistency And Update Contract
description:
User story: As a user, I want graph state to update when items change in app or on disk.

Preserve existing behavior and use docs/qml-frontend-migration-plan.md plus the approved capability baseline. Do not change unrelated production behavior or remove a Widgets workflow without explicit approval.
acceptance_criteria: Reflect successful local item/document/link/review changes and existing watcher events in the graph within 1 second; maintain consistency with tree/editor under stale events, errors and rebuilds; tests measure event-to-visible latency and do not introduce another watcher.
notes: User agreed visible updates within 1 second after successful local edits and external changes delivered by the existing watcher. Do not implement a second watcher; validate the target with measured project fixtures.

title: Optional Qml Graph Explorer
description:
User story: As a user, I want an optional knowledge-graph view to explore requirement relationships.

Preserve existing behavior and use docs/qml-frontend-migration-plan.md plus the approved capability baseline. Do not change unrelated production behavior or remove a Widgets workflow without explicit approval.
acceptance_criteria: Provide accessible pan/zoom/select, filtering and search based on approved competency questions; selecting a node navigates to existing tree/editor and back; graph does not replace existing navigation or edit workflows.

title: Graph Scale Storage And Interoperability
description:
User story: As a user, I want graph behavior to remain responsive and data ownership clear on large projects.

Preserve existing behavior and use docs/qml-frontend-migration-plan.md plus the approved capability baseline. Do not change unrelated production behavior or remove a Widgets workflow without explicit approval.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark representative large projects; keep v1 graph in memory and rebuildable from Doorstop; do not introduce persistent graph/cache, graph database or standard serialization in v1; record concrete triggers for revisiting these decisions; avoid blocking UI and document data/privacy behavior.
notes: User decided v1 graph is in-memory and derived from Doorstop; no persistent graph/cache, graph database or RDF/OWL/JSON-LD export in v1. Revisit only against a concrete persistence/interoperability use-case.
